correctness.rationale: The proof reduces quadratic forms by Frobenius-stable linear changes; derives rank-one and rank-two operators from explicit monomial chains; reconstructs the ternary modular Jordan spectrum from the classical finite-characteristic tensor rule and an explicit parity progression count; counts symmetric matrices of ranks zero through three; and removes all higher-degree corrections to a nonsingular quadratic by degree-by-degree filtered coordinate substitutions. The block sizes sum to p^3 and distinct types identify all four ranks. The standalone finite-field matrix checker exhausts 729 ternary quadratics in F_3, samples F_5 and F_7, tests higher-order nonsingular lifts and checks modular-fusion arithmetic up to p=19. These tests are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: The degree-two augmentation layer in the regular group algebra of (C_p)^3 is a canonical six-dimensional family of modular operators. The theorem completely classifies its Jordan types and multiplicities over every odd finite field, detects quadratic rank from the operator, and proves that every nonsingular higher-degree lift shares an unexpectedly rigid block structure. The projective-block multiplicity jumps from p at quadratic rank two to (p²+1)/2 at rank three. These are natural structural invariants not a numerical slice or a known-table recomputation, and address operators not captured by linear p-point restrictions.
